basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 29.' and it opens '(Vers. 29.) Ecce septem anni venient abundantiae magnae in omni terra Aegypti. Miror'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 29.) Ecce septem anni venient abundantiae magnae in omni terra Aegypti. Miror quomodo verbum Hebraicum (שבע) SABEE, quod nos supra, abundantiam, sive satietatem, in puteo quem foderunt extremum servi Isaac, interpretati sumus: nunc Septuaginta rectissime transferentes, ibi juramentum interpretati sunt, cum et juramentum, et septem, et satietas, et abundantia, prout locus et ordo flagitaverint, possit intelligi. Sed et in consequentibus ubicumque abundantia legitur, in Hebraeo idem verbum scriptum est.
